title: AI agent access
intro: What AI agents connected through the MCP server may do in this cluster. Nothing is allowed until you choose a set.

description.off: The agent has no access to this cluster. It sees the cluster in its list, but every call is refused.
description.readOnly: The agent can read all resources in all namespaces and fetch pod logs. Secret values are hidden. It cannot change anything.
description.readWrite: The agent can read everything and fetch logs, and can also change resources, run commands in containers and open port forwards. It asks you first each time. It cannot delete. Secret values are hidden.
description.full: The agent can do everything in all namespaces, including deleting. Changes, deletes, commands and port forwards ask you first each time. Secret values are hidden.
description.custom: You decide: each rule covers namespaces, kinds and actions. An action is allowed when at least one rule covers it.

customizeHint: Choose Custom to start from this set's rules and edit them.

unrecognised.notice: These rules were written by a newer Sextant or edited by hand; they are kept but not applied. The agent has no access until you reset to Off or choose a set, which replaces them.

saveFailed: Could not save the access rules.

rules.title: Rules
rules.none: There are no rules, so the agent has no access to this cluster.

namespaces.empty: No namespace is selected, so this rule covers nothing.
namespaces.clusterOnly: Resources that belong to no namespace (nodes, namespaces, CRDs, cluster roles) are covered only by a rule with all namespaces.

kinds.invalid: Use Kind or group/Kind, for example Pod or apps/Deployment.
kinds.empty: No kind is selected, so this rule covers nothing.
kinds.more: Showing the first {{count}}. Type in the filter to narrow the list.

picker.notConnected: Connect to this cluster to choose from its list. You can still type a name below.
picker.failed: The cluster's list is unavailable. You can still type a name below.

confirm.label: Ask before running
confirm.hint: Modify, Delete, Exec and Port forward in this rule wait for your answer in Sextant (120 s, then they are refused).

secretWarning: Secret values lets the agent read Secret data and the values of Helm releases in clear text. Only allow it for namespaces the agent really needs.

reviews.label: Let agents see my effective permissions
reviews.hint: An agent may then ask the Kubernetes API what your credentials for this cluster may do (a SelfSubjectRulesReview) in the namespaces it may read, and gets the answer cut to the kinds its rules cover. Useful when your RBAC is limited and the Roles cannot be read.
